The change is proposed, not final. The Super Emitter Program behind those reports started in 2024. It is one of several monitoring tools the agency uses, and officials say it can find problems that routine monitoring misses.

segments.text: For several years the Environmental Protection Agency has run a program that collects reports about large methane releases at oil and gas sites across the country. The Super Emitter Program started in 2024. It is one of several monitoring tools the agency uses, and officials say it can find problems that routine monitoring misses. Under the proposal, reports of company emissions detected by third parties would stop reaching EPA. Residents near these sites could lose an early warning, an estimated effect. The change is proposed, not final.
TEST DATA: For now this is a proposal, not a final rule, and residents can still comment on it.
